subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox prune does not clean up workspace directory

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the linked conflicting fork fix for this focused prune-workspace cleanup, or fold the work into the broader managed sandbox lifecycle issue?
rationale: The bug remains clear, but the cleanup deletes sandbox state and an unmerged linked fix candidate plus a broader maintainer lifecycle issue make the repair route a human ownership choice.

options.title: Land a narrow prune cleanup
options.body: Adopt or replace the linked branch with a focused fix that deletes only eligible non-shared local sandbox workspaces after successful runtime removal and adds regression tests.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle work
options.body: Keep this issue open as supporting context and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98516 define the permanent cleanup policy before changing prune behavior.

options.title: Close the stale fork candidate first
options.body: Close or supersede the conflicting fork PR before allowing a new repair job so there is one canonical implementation path.

recommendation.title: Land a narrow prune cleanup
recommendation.body: Adopt or replace the linked branch with a focused fix that deletes only eligible non-shared local sandbox workspaces after successful runtime removal and adds regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The sandbox lifecycle and prune behavior history points most strongly to Peter Steinberger's prior sandbox ownership and the broader related lifecycle issue.
